Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the annual independent test of the sanctions compliance program as an Internal Audit engagement; escalates critical/high findings to the Audit Committee and the AML/OFAC Compliance Officer

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — OFAC A Framework for Compliance Commitments (May 2019), Testing and Auditing pillar, re-read at each annual audit-plan refresh; cross-checked against the FFIEC BSA/AML Examination Manual OFAC section and 31 CFR Chapter V

In-scope processes.value: The full sanctions compliance program across all lines including Variable Insurance Products: sanctions list ingestion and currency, screening tool configuration and matching thresholds, alert generation and disposition, true-hit escalation, and blocked/rejected transaction reporting

In-scope systems.value: Screening engine and its list-ingestion/configuration modules, plus the NICE Actimize (AML) alert case-management workflow that queues and dispositions screening hits; engagement evidence staged in AuditBoard

Compliance procedure documented.value: Independent Testing of the Sanctions Compliance Program procedure (Internal Audit methodology) — scope-setting, list-currency check, configuration walkthrough, alert sampling and re-performance, root-cause and remediation tracking

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Audit Executive and ratified by the Audit Committee as part of the annual risk-based audit plan; reviewed annually or on any material OFAC enforcement action affecting the industry

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual — the test must complete and the report reach the Audit Committee and the AML/OFAC Compliance Officer no later than 12 months after the prior test's report date, per the OFAC Framework's periodic-testing cadence

Deadline reminders configured.value: AuditBoard audit-plan milestones at T-90/T-60/T-30 days to the report due date, plus calendar holds for fieldwork start, fieldwork close and Audit Committee reporting

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Engagement workpapers, list-currency and configuration extracts, alert sample dispositions, findings log and the final report retained 5 years from issuance in the compliance evidence repository, consistent with 31 CFR 501.601 recordkeeping

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every audit finding logged as a tracker issue with severity, root cause and a remediation owner/date; findings repeated from the prior year's test are flagged as escalated

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs the management response on every finding — concurrence with a committed remediation date, or a documented rebuttal with supporting evidence — before the report is finalized

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All screening-list update events, screening configuration states, and all sanctions-screening alerts (true and false hit) generated across every source feed during the current test period, plus every blocked/rejected transaction report filed with OFAC in that period

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on list-currency lag beyond one business day; screening configuration must match the approved baseline with no undocumented deviations; sampled alert dispositions and blocked-transaction reports must be 100% correct and timely; any miss is a formal finding with a remediation plan

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation and independent test are both annual; the test is performed once per calendar year by Internal Audit, separate from and in addition to the program's own daily automated screening cycle

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer signs off the QA re-performance and did not staff the original engagement's fieldwork

Evidence location for test results.value: QA workpaper, re-performance notes and the final conclusion filed in AuditBoard under the annual sanctions-program engagement, mirrored to the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Final audit report packaged with the list-currency log, configuration baseline comparison and alert-sample workpapers, presentable to OFAC or a state/federal examiner within 5 business days of request

Regulator response path.value: AML/OFAC Compliance Officer and General Counsel jointly own any regulator inquiry into test results; the Chief Audit Executive briefs the Audit Committee before any external release

checklist.step: Scope and schedule the annual independent test of the sanctions compliance program
actions: Open AuditBoard's Annual Audit Plan and create/confirm the engagement 'Sanctions Compliance Program — Independent Test' for the current cycle.

Set scope to the three OFAC Framework pillars named in the obligation: screening tool configuration, sanctions list currency, and alert handling/disposition, plus blocked/rejected transaction reporting.
Confirm engagement independence: exclude any auditor who administers or configures the screening tool or dispositions alerts from the engagement team.
Set fieldwork start/close dates and the report-issuance date so the report reaches the Audit Committee within 12 months of the prior test.
Route the engagement scope memo to the Audit Committee chair and the AML/OFAC Compliance Officer for concurrence before fieldwork opens.
checklist.done: the engagement is opened in AuditBoard with scope, independent staffing and a report date inside the 12-month cadence, concurred by the Audit Committee chair.

checklist.step: Gather the current sanctions program governance package
actions: Request from the Financial Crime AML Officer the current Sanctions Compliance Policy, the OFAC screening procedure, the escalation matrix and the list of screened business lines (policy issuance, claims payment, premium receipt, agent/producer onboarding, variable product subaccount transfers).
Pull the prior year's independent test report and open remediation tracker items from AuditBoard.
Obtain the approved screening-configuration baseline document and its most recent change-control approval.
Request the org chart and RACI for sanctions screening administration, Tier 1/Tier 2 alert review, and true-hit escalation.
File the governance package in the engagement workpaper folder.
checklist.done: the current policy, procedure, escalation matrix, configuration baseline and prior-year remediation status are on file in the engagement folder.

checklist.step: Verify sanctions list currency and update cadence
actions: In the screening system open Administration ▸ List Management and pull the ingest log for the SDN List, the Consolidated Sanctions List, the Sectoral Sanctions Identifications (SSI) List and every applicable country/program list for the test period.
Cross-reference each ingest timestamp against OFAC's published list-update notifications (ofac.treasury.gov Recent Actions) for the same period.
Compute the lag in hours between OFAC publication and system ingestion for every update event.
Flag any update where the lag exceeds one business day and record the cause (vendor feed delay, manual load, outage).
Screenshot the ingest log and the corresponding OFAC publication notice for each tested update into the workpaper.
checklist.done: every list update in the test period has a computed lag, and any lag over one business day is flagged with a documented cause.

checklist.step: Review screening tool configuration against the approved baseline
actions: In the screening system open Administration ▸ Matching Configuration and record the current fuzzy-match algorithm, sensitivity/threshold score, and the fields screened (name, alias, date of birth, address, entity identifiers, vessel IMO/BIC where applicable).
Compare each setting to the approved configuration baseline document gathered in Step 2.
For any variance, pull the change-control ticket in the GRC platform (Archer/ServiceNow GRC) and confirm it carries an approval from the Financial Crime AML Officer and a tested-impact assessment.
Note any configuration change made without a change-control ticket as an unauthorized-change finding.
checklist.done: live configuration matches the approved baseline, and every deviation is traced to an approved, tested change-control ticket.

checklist.step: Confirm screening coverage across every in-scope transaction type and line of business
actions: List every source system feeding the screening engine: Guidewire PolicyCenter (new business/renewal named insureds), Guidewire ClaimCenter (claimants and payees), Guidewire BillingCenter (premium payers), the agency/producer management system (appointed producers) and the variable insurance product subaccount transfer feed.

For each feed, confirm in the screening system's interface configuration that the feed is active, mapped to the correct party-role fields, and screening on both onboarding and every transaction event, not just point-in-time.
Pull a sample transaction from each feed and confirm a corresponding screening record exists with a timestamp at or before the transaction's effective date.
Record any feed found inactive, unmapped or screening only a subset of party roles as a coverage gap finding.
checklist.done: every named source feed is confirmed active and correctly mapped, with a traced sample transaction proving screening actually ran.

checklist.step: Pull the full population of screening alerts generated in the test period
actions: In NICE Actimize open the Alert Management workspace and export all sanctions-screening alerts (true and false hit dispositions) generated within the test period, across all lines of business.
Include alert id, source feed, match score, disposition, disposition date, disposition owner and any escalation reference on the export.
Reconcile the exported alert count to the screening system's own alert-generation log for the same period and resolve any count difference before sampling.
Save the reconciled population extract into the engagement workpaper.
checklist.done: the alert population is exported, reconciled to the screening system's generation log, and filed as the sampling universe.

checklist.step: Draw a risk-based sample of alerts for disposition testing
actions: Take 100% of alerts dispositioned as true hits or escalated to the Financial Crime AML Officer.
Take a random, seeded sample of 25 false-hit dispositions from the remaining population, minimum 40 alerts total.
Stratify the random sample to include at least one alert from each in-scope source feed.
Record the seed, population size and sample date in the workpaper so the sample is reproducible.
checklist.done: the sample includes every true hit/escalation, a reproducible random draw of false hits, and coverage of every source feed.

checklist.step: Re-perform the disposition call on each sampled alert
actions: Reopen each sampled alert in NICE Actimize and independently review the underlying name/DOB/address/entity match against the sanctions list entry, without reading the recorded disposition first.
Reach an independent true-hit/false-hit conclusion and record the reasoning.
Compare the independent conclusion to the recorded disposition; log any disagreement as an exception, including cases where the final call was right but the documented rationale was insufficient.
For true hits, confirm the alert was escalated to the Financial Crime AML Officer within the SLA stated in the escalation matrix.
checklist.done: every sampled alert has an independent re-performance conclusion compared to the recorded disposition, with disagreements logged as exceptions.

checklist.step: Test blocked and rejected transaction reporting to OFAC
actions: For every true-hit/blocked transaction in the sample, confirm a blocking report was prepared identifying the blocked property per 31 CFR 501.603.
Confirm the report was filed within 10 business days of the blocking action, and that any rejection was reported within the required timeframe under 31 CFR 501.604.
Confirm the transaction and the underlying blocked property were added to the OFAC annual comprehensive report of blocked property, due by September 30 each year covering the prior calendar year.
File the filing confirmation and submitted report copy into the engagement workpaper.
checklist.done: every blocked/rejected transaction in the sample traces to a timely 501.603/501.604 report and, where applicable, inclusion in the annual blocked-property report.

checklist.step: Assess alert queue timeliness and backlog
actions: Pull the alert aging report from NICE Actimize showing open alert count and days-open distribution as of each month-end in the test period.
Compare average and maximum days-to-disposition against the SLA in the escalation matrix gathered in Step 2.
Identify any month where the open-alert backlog grew month over month and request the root cause from the Sanctions Analyst.
Record backlog trend and SLA breach counts in the workpaper.
checklist.done: backlog and SLA-breach metrics are pulled for every month in the period, with root cause obtained for any growing backlog.

checklist.step: Interview control owners on program operation
actions: Interview the Financial Crime AML Officer on true-hit escalation practice, false-positive tuning history and any near-miss incidents in the period.
Interview the Sanctions Analyst on day-to-day alert handling, list-update verification and any manual workarounds used when the screening system was degraded.
Document interview notes with date, attendee and key statements in the workpaper.
Corroborate any statement that conflicts with the sampled evidence and note the conflict as a finding.
checklist.done: interview notes are on file for both control owners, with any conflict against sampled evidence flagged.

checklist.step: Draft findings with root cause and severity
actions: Consolidate every exception from the list-currency, configuration, alert-sample, blocked-reporting and backlog steps into a findings log with a severity rating (Critical/High/Medium/Low) based on sanctions-breach potential.
Assign a root cause category to each finding: list-feed delay, configuration drift, disposition error, reporting-timeliness miss, or backlog/resourcing.
Draft a proposed remediation action and target date for each finding.
Route the draft findings log to the Chief Audit Executive for quality review before management discussion.
checklist.done: every exception is consolidated into a severity-rated, root-caused finding with a proposed remediation and target date.

checklist.step: Validate findings with the process owner and obtain management response
actions: Review each draft finding against the underlying evidence and either concur or provide a documented rebuttal with supporting evidence.
For concurred findings, commit a remediation owner and date, entered directly on the finding.
For rebutted findings, provide the countervailing evidence to Internal Audit within 5 business days for re-assessment.
Sign the management response section of the findings log.
checklist.done: every finding carries a signed management response — concurrence with a committed remediation, or a documented, evidence-backed rebuttal.

checklist.step: Report results to the Audit Committee and the AML/OFAC Compliance Officer
actions: Assemble the final report: scope, population, sample results, findings with severity and root cause, management responses and overall program conclusion.
Upload the report to the board portal ahead of the next scheduled Audit Committee meeting.
Present the report to the Audit Committee, highlighting any Critical/High findings and any use-before-remediation sanctions exposure.
Distribute the final report to the AML/OFAC Compliance Officer and General Counsel the same day it is presented.
checklist.done: the final report is on the board portal, presented to the Audit Committee and distributed to the AML/OFAC Compliance Officer and General Counsel.

checklist.step: Track remediation to closure and retain the engagement evidence
actions: Log each committed remediation action into AuditBoard's issue tracker with owner, target date and current status.
Follow up at each target date and request closure evidence (updated configuration screenshot, revised procedure, retrained staff attestation) from the Financial Crime AML Officer.

Move the full engagement folder (governance package, population extracts, sample workpapers, findings log, report, closure evidence) into the compliance evidence repository under the current test-year tag.
Apply a 5-year retention label consistent with 31 CFR 501.601 recordkeeping and confirm the repository index is searchable by finding id and remediation status.
checklist.done: every remediation item is tracked to closure evidence and the full engagement record is retained for 5 years and searchable by finding id.

testing.step: Build the population of the current-year engagement's workpapers and findings
actions: Pull all workpapers from the annual sanctions-program engagement in AuditBoard.
List every planned audit step from the approved engagement scope and confirm each has a corresponding evidenced workpaper.
Reconcile the step count executed to the approved audit program and resolve any gap before QA testing.
Flag any planned step skipped, undocumented, or evidenced with a placeholder rather than real support.
testing.done: the population of engagement steps and findings is reconciled to the approved audit program with no unexplained gaps.

testing.step: Reconcile the alert sample drawn by the engagement to the actual alert population
actions: Independently re-extract the full-period alert population from NICE Actimize using the same date range and scope as the engagement.
Compare the independently extracted count and date range to the population the engagement documented.
Recompute the sample using the recorded seed and confirm it reproduces the same alert ids as the engagement's documented sample.
Log any discrepancy in population count or sample reproducibility as an exception.
testing.done: the independently re-extracted population and reproduced sample match the engagement's documentation, or the difference is logged.

testing.step: Recompute the sanctions list currency lag independently
actions: Pull OFAC's published list-update timestamps for the test period directly from ofac.treasury.gov Recent Actions.
Independently pull the screening system's list-ingest log for the same period.
Recompute the lag in hours for each update and compare the result to the lag figures recorded in the engagement workpaper.
Flag any variance in the recomputed lag, and any update the engagement failed to test.
testing.done: the recomputed lag for every list update matches the engagement's figures, or the variance is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Re-perform disposition on a subset of the sampled alerts
actions: Reopen a subset of the engagement's sampled alerts in the case management queue without reading the engagement's re-performance notes first.
Independently reach a true/false-hit conclusion using the same name/DOB/entity matching criteria the screening procedure requires.
Compare the independent conclusion to the engagement's documented re-performance conclusion.
Treat any disagreement, including a difference in supporting rationale, as a QA exception.
testing.done: the independent second re-performance agrees with the engagement's documented conclusion on every subset alert, or disagreements are logged.

testing.step: Verify screening configuration evidence against the approved baseline
actions: Pull the configuration baseline document version referenced in the engagement workpaper.
Compare the live-system configuration screenshot dates captured by the engagement to the baseline's approval date.
Confirm any configuration change occurring during the test period has a matching change-control ticket in the GRC platform (Archer/ServiceNow GRC).
Flag any configuration comparison the engagement did not evidence with a dated screenshot.
testing.done: every configuration comparison in the engagement is supported by a dated screenshot and a matching change-control ticket where applicable.

testing.step: Trace blocked/rejected transaction handling to the underlying OFAC reporting obligations
actions: For every true-hit/blocked transaction in the engagement's sample, confirm a report was prepared and filed per 31 CFR 501.603/501.604.
Trace the report to the OFAC report file and its submission confirmation.
Recompute the filing deadline (10 business days from the blocking action, and the annual comprehensive blocked-property report due September 30) against the actual filing date.
Log any transaction where the recomputed deadline was missed or where the engagement's workpaper lacked the submission confirmation.
testing.done: every sampled blocked/rejected transaction traces to a report filed within the recomputed deadline, or the miss is logged.

testing.step: Check remediation tracking for the prior year's findings
actions: Pull the prior year's finding log from AuditBoard.
Confirm each prior finding has an owner, a remediation date and closure evidence attached.
Verify any finding still open was carried into the current year's engagement scope as a mandatory retest item.
Flag any finding marked closed without supporting closure evidence.
testing.done: every prior-year finding is either evidenced closed or carried forward as a mandatory retest in the current engagement.

testing.step: Confirm reporting and Audit Committee escalation occurred on time
actions: Pull the Audit Committee meeting minutes and materials referencing the sanctions-program test.
Confirm the report presentation date falls within 12 months of the prior test's report date.
Confirm the AML/OFAC Compliance Officer and General Counsel were copied on the report per the escalation path.
Flag any gap between the required cadence and the actual reporting date.
testing.done: the report reached the Audit Committee within the 12-month cadence and was distributed to the AML/OFAC Compliance Officer and General Counsel.

testing.step: Log every QA exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue for each QA exception identified in the recomputation, re-performance and reconciliation steps.
Assign a root cause (missing evidence, sampling error, recomputation variance, late reporting) and an owner for each.
Set a remediation date and, for any confirmed use-before-approval or missed-reporting exception, open a self-assessment referral to the AML/OFAC Compliance Officer.
Carry every open QA exception into the next year's engagement scope as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every QA exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the QA review
actions: Compute the QA exception rate across all re-performed and recomputed items.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) referencing the specific evidence behind it.
Sign the QA workpaper as the reviewer segregated from the original engagement's fieldwork team.
Report the QA conclusion to the Audit Committee and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed QA workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and Audit Committee reporting date exists in the compliance evidence repository.
